findings.reason: The protected app-local and Accepted native sources use the prohibited generic local name `index` for the range cursor. The candidate preserves their optimal maximal-run scan and app-local contract while using the conventional interview variable `i`.

Apart from the naming issue, the protected algorithm is already direct and optimal: it advances each input position once, emits only maximal range endpoints, uses O(n) time, and needs O(1) auxiliary space beyond the required result. No algorithmic rewrite or micro-optimization is justified.

The former 8/64/256-value benchmark violated the source limit of 20 values. Legal 5/10/20-value singleton-range tiers now span 4x and maximize the output path. The candidate passes at +0.02 relative exponent; a correct implementation that rescans the full input for every range passes every output and fails only scaling at +0.63.

The Approach now describes the candidate's `i` cursor exactly, states the maximal-run argument and O(1) auxiliary-space convention precisely, and labels empty-input and integer-boundary behavior explicitly.
